subject: MAP: Capacity matchmaking & evaluation milestones — Verdant Labs
body:
From: Alex Monroe <alex@verdant.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Capacity matchmaking & evaluation milestones — Verdant Labs

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Verdant is excited to move forward but procurement and our infra team need clarity on lead times and how GPU pool sizing fits into the MAP.

Top asks from our side:
- Target close window (we're hoping for end of Q4).
- Typical Dedicated/Private lead times for reserved capacity (H100-equivalent).
- A recommended starting GPU pool size for our anticipated workload (batch embed + low-latency chat at ~250 req/s peak).
- Any gating items (SOC2 evidence, network requirements) that will slow acceptance.

Can you put together a short MAP-style timeline that ties eval milestones to reservation milestones? Procurement also requested an example acceptance matrix.

Appreciate it — Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Verdant Labs

---
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Monroe <alex@verdant.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity matchmaking & evaluation milestones — Verdant Labs

Alex,

Great to hear — and appreciate the clarity on asks. I sketched a MAP that ties the evaluation gates to reservation triggers. High level notes below; I attached a one-tab MAP skeleton as well and can expand.

Quick answers up front:
- Close target: we can support an end-of-Q4 contractual close (formal reservation) if we get a signed MSA + initial PO by 2027-11-20.
- Lead times: for Dedicated pools with H100-equivalent capacity, procurement to delivery (cloud-dedicated) is typically 6–8 weeks after we receipt the PO; Private/on-prem runs longer due to hardware and network (14–18 weeks) unless you opt for a staged hybrid (reserved headroom in hosted then physical on-prem later).
- Sizing: For 250 req/s peak (95th pct), recommended starting pool is 8 H100-equivalents with a 2x KV-cache buffer for chat workloads; for embeddings-heavy batch jobs we recommend a separate burstable pool or on-demand overlay.
- Gating items: SOC2 evidence, network IP allowlist, VPC peering details, and model quantization acceptance for latency SLAs.

I want to align on a short MAP with the following checkpoints:
1) Eval plan (2 weeks): POC tokens, sample prompts, latency and throughput targets.
2) Reservation decision (1 week): sign MSA + PO; select Dedicated vs Private.
3) Procurement/Provisioning (6–18 weeks depending on mode).
4) Onboarding & acceptance (2–4 weeks): SLA verifications, load validation, runbook handoff.

Attaching: Verdant_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP skeleton). I will loop in Ben for the pool-sizing breakdown and Chloe to draft an acceptance matrix you can hand to procurement.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity matchmaking & evaluation milestones — Verdant Labs

Alex / Soojin — quick sizing addendum based on their stated profile.

If Verdant's traffic shape is 70% chat (low token per call, latency-sensitive) and 30% batch embeddings (heavy but parallelizable), the 8 H100-equivalent starting point is reasonable with the following profile:
- Live lane: 6 GPUs dedicated to low-latency chat, with async KV-cache warmed for top prefixes.
- Batch lane: 2 GPUs, larger batch sizes and quantized model for cost efficiency.
- Autoscaling: enable burst capacity up to +50% for initial 8-week ramp.

Operational notes: Reserved Dedicated pools are pinned to capacity; we recommend a 3-month performance review to decide whether to shift capacity between lanes. Lead time note: ordering more than 12 GPUs or requesting a private on-prem deployment with hardware procurement will push delivery toward the 14–18 week window Soojin mentioned.

I've also added a rough cost delta in the MAP workbook.

-Ben
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Alex — attaching the MAP workbook with an added Acceptance Matrix tab and a short checklist for procurement (SOC2 checklist + network requirements). See attached: Verdant_MAP_v1.xlsx (tabs: MAP, Acceptance Matrix, Cost Delta).

Acceptance Matrix highlights (examples):
- CPU/GPU availability: confirm Dedicated pool meets 99.5% weekday availability for 4–6 hour business windows.
- Latency gate: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms for chat at 95th percentile traffic.
- Token accounting: sample token-based billing tests pass and match estimated invoices to within 10%.
- Security gate: SOC2 summary received + IP allowlist validated.

Action items (short):
1) Verdant: confirm preferred deployment mode (Dedicated or Private) by 2027-11-10.
2) Verdant: share sample prompts and a small representative dataset for eval by 2027-11-03.
3) Redwood: produce final reservation lead time table and PO template by 2027-11-12.

Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Monroe <alex@verdant.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@verdant.ai>, chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Capacity matchmaking & evaluation milestones — Verdant Labs

Alex / Priya — thanks for the SOC2 bundle and the quick clarifying Qs. Final alignment from Redwood below so procurement has a clear checklist and timeline to act on.

1) Test harness: Redwood will provide a portable test harness (containerized) and a reference dataset so Verdant can run the same latency/throughput tests in their staging environment. We will also run a mirrored test from our Dedicated pool; both runs will be part of Acceptance.

2) Staged approach: supported. Recommended path for a short runway close:
   a) Stage 1 (Hosted Dedicated overlay) — provision Dedicated headroom in our hosted fleet to hit your Q4 SLAs within 2–3 weeks after PO receipt. This minimizes customer-facing risk while hardware for Private is procured.
   b) Stage 2 (Private/on-prem) — hardware procurement and on-prem install (14–18 week lead time). Data plane migration planned as a drift-managed cutover.

Pricing note: staged approach will be priced as a two-part agreement — a short-term Hosted Dedicated commitment (discounted for bridging) and a later Private transition addendum (credits applied for overlapping months). We'll provide a worked example in the PO template.

3) Concrete MAP milestones and dates (actionable — target close end-of-Q4):
   - 2027-11-03: Verdant delivers sample prompts + dataset for eval (pending — please confirm).
   - 2027-11-10: Verdant confirms deployment mode (Dedicated preferred; indicate Private intent if you want hardware procurement queued).
   - 2027-11-12: Redwood delivers final reservation lead time table and PO template (we will include staged pricing options).
   - 2027-11-20: Target for signed MSA + initial PO (this triggers Hosted Dedicated overlay provisioning).
   - 2027-11-22 to 2028-01-10: Provisioning window (Hosted Dedicated overlay live within 2–3 weeks; private hardware 14–18 weeks if requested).
   - 2028-01-15 to 2028-01-31: Acceptance window; run mirrored test harness and finalize SLA sign-off.

4) Attachments: Verdant_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + Acceptance Matrix) and SOC2-summary.pdf received.

Next immediate asks for Verdant (please):
- Confirm delivery of sample prompts by 2027-11-03 and preferred deployment mode by 2027-11-10.
- Procurement: please share your PO template or procurement constraints; we will mirror any specific purchase order fields in our PO template.

I'll drop an updated MAP packet into the Drive link and post the PO template by 2027-11-12. If procurement wants a brief call to walk the acceptance matrix, Chloe and I are available next week (Nov 15–17).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this locked.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
